{{Current events|year=2022|month=01|day=28|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
**[[Russia–NATO relations]]
***[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Minister]] [[Sergey Lavrov]] says that [[Russia]] is not interested in starting a war after [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] warned [[Ukraine]] that Russia may invade Ukraine in February. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/rcna13921 (NBC News)]
***At a special [[The Pentagon|Pentagon]] [[press briefing]], [[United States Army]] [[General (United States)|General]] [[Mark Milley]] and [[United States Secretary of Defense|Secretary of Defense]] [[Lloyd Austin]] warn that a Russian invasion of Ukraine would be "horrific" and could result in "significant casualties". [https://www.reuters.com/world/horrific-destruction-casualties-if-russia-invades-ukraine-us-2022-01-28/ (Reuters)]
**[[Belarus–NATO relations]]
***[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that [[Belarus]] might go to war if they or Russia are attacked. Lukashenko also insists that his country does not want to go to war with Ukraine. [https://www.politico.eu/article/russia-alexander-lukashenko-belarus-ukraine-conflict-crisis/amp/ (Politico EU)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**[[2022 Kech District attack]]
***Ten [[Pakistan Army]] soldiers are killed in an [[insurgent]] attack in [[Kech District]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. The [[separatist]] [[Baluch Liberation Front]] claims responsibility for the attack. The army says that it has killed one of the attackers and arrested three others in a clearance operation. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/ten-pakistani-soldiers-killed-insurgent-attack-army-says-2022-01-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Chinese espionage in the United States]]
**The [[Federal Communications Commission]] votes unanimously to revoke the authorisation of [[China Unicom]] to operate in the [[United States]], citing national security and [[espionage]] concerns. The [[China|Chinese]] [[telecommunications]] operator must stop providing telecoms services in the U.S. within 60 days. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-60164747 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The [[Fern Hollow Bridge]] in [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[United States]], collapses, causing a gas leak. Ten people are injured, none of them seriously. [https://www.post-gazette.com/local/city/2022/01/28/pittsburgh-bridge-collapse-forbes-braddock-avenue-point-breeze-squirrel-hill/stories/202201280075 (''Pittsburgh Post-Gazette'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Department of Tourism (Philippines)|Philippine Department of Tourism]] announces the lifting of quarantine requirements for fully [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated]] tourists from countries under [[Visa policy of the Philippines#Visa waiver program|its visa waiver program]], effective February 10. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/philippines-to-reopen-for-fully-vaccinated-foreign-tourists-in-february-2734592 (AFP via NDTV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 16,096 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 793,582. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20220128004255320 (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 228,954 new COVID-19 cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 24.7 million. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/international/brazil-s-daily-covid-19-caseload-rises-by-record-228-954-infections-122012800137_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
****[[Chile]] reports a record 26,727 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.075 million. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/20220129/4de2cd799ca747c3be138267cf71498a/c.html#:~:text=SANTIAGO%2C%20Jan.%2028%20(Xinhua,Ministry%20of%20Health%20said%20Friday. (Xinhua News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****[[New South Wales]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] BA.2 sublineage. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jan/28/australia-records-deadliest-day-of-covid-pandemic-as-35-cases-of-ba2-omicron-variant-detected (''The Guardian'')]
***[[Australia]] reports a record 98 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, including a record 35 deaths in [[New South Wales]]. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/australia-has-recorded-its-largest-daily-number-of-covid-19-deaths/f6b37f93-8641-4377-bb1c-c40024f7c4e9 (SBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record for the eighth consecutive day of 98,040 new [[COVID-19]] cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 11.5 million. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/russia-nears-100000-daily-infections-omicron-rages-82529394 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2022 Burkinabé coup d'état]]
**The leaders of the [[Economic Community of West African States]] agree to suspend [[Burkina Faso]]'s membership in the bloc in response to the [[coup d'état]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/w-africa-bloc-suspends-post-coup-burkina (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Foreign relations of Rwanda]], [[Foreign relations of Uganda]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (Rwanda)|Rwandan foreign ministry]] announces the reopening of [[Rwanda|the country]]'s border crossing with [[Uganda]] following political tensions between the two countries that led to the closure of the border crossing for three years. [http://www.seychellesnewsagency.com/articles/16207/Rwanda+to+reopen+Uganda+land+border+after+three-year+closure (AFP via Seychelles News Agency)]
